## `make verify` caught a defect in this change; fixed and amended

First full verify run: **1 failed, 20,099 passed, 27 skipped** in 43:21.

```
FAILED tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_tool_surface_golden.py::test_live_surface_equals_golden[plan_review_status]
```

### What was wrong

This change edits the `plan_review_status` docstring in `src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py` to drop `` ``not-closed`` `` from the verdict list. Removing that token shortens a line, so the paragraph re-wraps. The companion golden entry in `tests/interfaces/facades/mcp_tool_surface_golden.json` was **hand-edited to match** rather than recaptured from the live surface, and the hand edit got the re-wrap wrong in two places:

| | source docstring (correct) | golden as committed (wrong) |
|---|---|---|
| signature-failure list | `` (``mismatch``, ``invalid``, ``foreign_key``, ``unavailable``,\n`` | `` ``foreign_key``,\n        ``unavailable``, …`` — an extra break after `foreign_key` |
| closing sentence | `` names the drift; the SHA\n        and timestamp…`` | `` names the drift; the SHA and\n        timestamp…`` — the pre-change wrap, left unchanged |

The words are identical in both; only newline positions differ. That is exactly what this test exists to catch — it pins each tool's description **byte-for-byte**, so a reflow is a real surface change even though no client-visible text changed.

### Why the error was easy to make and hard to see

The golden is not generated by any script. `tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_tool_surface_golden.py` documents capture via an inline `python -c` one-liner in its module docstring; there is no `scripts/` entry point. So the only maintenance path is manual, and a manual re-wrap of a `\n`-escaped JSON string is error-prone in a way a regeneration step would not be. The second error is the more instructive one: that line needed re-wrapping *because* of the deletion, and it simply was not touched — the edit fixed the line containing the removed token and stopped there.

### The fix

Recaptured the single field from the live surface and replaced it as a unique string literal, so the file's `indent=1, sort_keys=True` serialization is otherwise untouched. Verified mechanically that **exactly one top-level entry** (`plan_review_status`) and **exactly one field within it** (`description`) differ from the committed version.

- `pytest tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_tool_surface_golden.py -q` → **68 passed**
- `git diff --stat` → `1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)`
- `make lint` → clean (zizmor and actionlint included)
- Checked the golden's other consumer: `src/rebar/_mcp_tool_specs.py` only **mentions** the file in its module docstring; it does not read it. The test is the sole real consumer, so the blast radius of this field is one test.

Amended onto the same commit — `Change-Id: I7be4ef8e40a03bdaaf19c1345fbaffc7c94ca47a` preserved, still 18 files, `e607f54110d`.

### Re-running the full verify rather than arguing from the partial run

The amended tree differs from the verified tree by one JSON string consumed by one test, and that test's whole file now passes. That is a strong argument, but it is not the same thing as a clean run, and this is the last child of epic `87d8-8bb6-5226-4a5b` — a wrong call here costs a `Verified -1` round trip plus a re-review. Full `make verify` is running against `e607f54110d`.
